extracted.intended_audience: diagnostic assay developers, public health researchers, and grant reviewers evaluating HIV incidence assay development
extracted.subtask_description: Optimization, validation, manufacturing scale-up, and field evaluation of a lateral-flow rapid HIV incidence (recency) test intended for population surveillance and potential diagnostic use. Includes analytical/clinical performance targets, stability/manufacturing/QC requirements, and validation study designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mean duration (ω) specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Key attribute: the mean duration (ω) — the time at which an individual converts from 'recent' to 'established' infection — must be defined for the assay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine ω for each subtype and overall; use seroconversion panels (ART‑naïve) to estimate biomarker kinetics and ω (recommended 20–30 panels per subtype A, B, C, D, AE, and/or other CRFs). For worldwide application, require statistically equivalent ω across subtypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: False recency rate (FRR) performance target
rubrics_metrics.description: The assay must minimize misclassification of longstanding infections as recent; the false recency rate (FRR) is a primary performance metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target FRR <2%. Evaluate FRR using >1 year (ART‑naïve) specimens, AIDS specimens, elite controllers, and individuals on ART. Guidance table indicates e.g. ~500 specimens per study population (for some FRR evaluations) and inclusion of at least 2–3 subtypes for FRR estimation. If FRR >2% in a given population, consider exclusion criteria or reflex/confirmatory RITA strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concordance with LAg ELISA / reference assay
rubrics_metrics.description: Assay results should correspond closely with the LAg ELISA (current standard) for Recent vs Long-Term classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary/prototype targets: >95% correspondence (text cites >95% and elsewhere >98% agreement for recent/long‑term classification). Validate across multiple panels and subtypes; account for potential cutoff differences when comparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability across HIV Group M subtypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Assay must provide equivalent results across widely circulating HIV Group M subtypes/clades to be suitable for worldwide use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize and test antigen formulation (rIDR-M or synthetic peptides) on panels representing major subtypes (A, B, C, D, AE, etc.). Demonstrate statistically equivalent ω and equivalent recency/long‑term classification across subtypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical sensitivity relative to ELISA
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical sensitivity should equal or exceed that of ELISAs using common HRP reagents and the best colorimetric substrates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prototype demonstrated detection of antibodies at ng/ml concentrations and positive signals at dilutions up to ~10 million for some samples; detection sensitivity should significantly exceed conventional colloidal gold/latex labels. Aim to match or exceed ELISA sensitivity (e.g., comparable TMB HRP performance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay run time (speed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rapid test must provide results in a short time suitable for field use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design targets: rapid (<15 minute) format; prototype achieved <12 minutes from sample application to result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay format: combined titer and avidity measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: The test should combine antibody titer and avidity analysis in a simple lateral flow format to discriminate recent versus long‑term infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a one-step avidity approach where the dissociation reagent is present during sample incubation to prevent low‑affinity binding (no separate dissociation and wash steps). Combine with two-antigen conjugate 'QuickELISA™' antibody-capture format to label and capture in one step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal positive control and scoring/chart interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an internal positive control line and a standardized scoring chart for visual interpretation of band patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal positive (red) line qualifies an assay as valid. Provide a score card/chart in the kit with representative high‑quality color images of pedigreed samples across recent→long‑term to guide interpretation; consider multiple band intensities (3 bands) for greater dynamic range and an interpretation spreadsheet/IFU and training materials for objective documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplexing & multi-color detection capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection chemistry should permit multi-color/multiplexed antibody detection for several peptide antigens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peroxidase-based multi‑color colorimetric detection (HRP + two-component substrate system) allowing distinct colors in multiple test zones (internal control + multiple test lines) to simplify visual readout or simple densitometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to analyze undiluted samples and multiple antibody classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Format should allow minimal or no sample dilution and detection of multiple antibody classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QuickELISA™ antibody-capture format (two peptide conjugates, no secondary antibody) enables detection with minimal dilution or undiluted serum and captures IgG, IgM and other multivalent antibody classes in a single assay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample matrix flexibility (serum/plasma/DBS/saliva)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and validate acceptable sample types and compare performance across matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary validation on serum/plasma; evaluate DBS and oral fluid/saliva (prototype showed correlated saliva/plasma detection) and compare serum vs plasma. Consider plasma separation devices and dried sample formats for field use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory validation requirements & sample/run counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory validation must demonstrate precision, applicability to subtypes, and reproducible performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimization stage: >100 runs on controls for lab validation. Assay precision target: %CV for controls <10% (in the dynamic range). Use manufacturer QC panels and defined pass criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seroconverter panels for MDR estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use seroconversion panels to derive biomarker kinetics and mean duration (ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend 20–30 seroconversion panels per subtype (A, B, C, D, AE, and other CRFs) to estimate ω per subtype and overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRR evaluation sample composition and sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: FRR must be estimated across relevant special populations and study sizes sufficient to characterize misclassification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess FRR in: >1 year (ART‑naïve) samples, AIDS cases, elite controllers (20–30 samples), and individuals on ART (50–100 samples minimum for at least 1 subtype). Some guidance suggests 500 specimens per study population for certain FRR assessments and inclusion of multiple subtypes (minimum 2–3) for FRR characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field validation design and population requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Field validation should compare assay-derived incidence estimates to modeled/observed incidence and evaluate operability and reproducibility in real-world settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct cross-sectional surveys in a minimum of 2–3 populations (containing the relevant subtype(s)); compare incidence estimates with other methods for plausibility. Perform operability evaluations at multiple field sites (e.g., two sites) with feedback used to refine IFU/training. Sub-category risk analyses should include minimum 2–3 survey populations; odds ratios should be plausible and comparable to observed risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing scale-up and pilot lot production
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop manufacturing processes and produce pilot lots to demonstrate consistent lot-to-lot performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce three pilot lots of ~1–2,000 cassettes each to support lab and field evaluations; optimize strip production steps (impregnation, dispensing, drying, cutting, laminating) and dispensing technologies (e.g., non-contact ink-jet). Maintain humidity control and follow GMP/ISO13485 controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lot verification and QC panel criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each lot must be verified with QC panels and pass stringent external QC criteria prior to release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a QC panel comprising 10–12 samples spanning incidence and prevalence sera plus negatives to verify performance of each lot. Develop QC criteria for peptide conjugates, substrate reagents, and dissociation reagents; establish in-process QA reagents/procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reagent and device stability targets and studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish stability profiles and target shelf life for reagents and assembled devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct real-time stability at 4°C and room temperature (20–25°C) and accelerated stability at 37°C. Target shelf life: 12 months at room temperature. Evaluate stability of dry reagent forms (substrate, dissociation reagent, conjugates) in assembled cassettes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dry-form reagent and dried-control development
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop stable dry forms of assay reagents and controls suitable for field kits and shipping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create dry peptide conjugates, dry dissociation reagent (for a separate sample application zone or dried format), and dry substrate reagents integrated into lateral flow cassettes. For kit controls, prepare dried tube specimens (air-dried vs lyophilized) and select an optimal protocol (lyophilization preferred for rapid reconstitution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Device design and cassette requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cassette and strip design must accommodate the novel detection chemistry and support simple, low-cost assembly and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design injection-molded cassette to manage fluid volume, diagnostic line placement, and delivery of peroxide substrate; consider two versions for dry substrate reagent vs liquid. Optimize diagnostic membrane/test line placement and three-line vs single-line configurations for discrimination. Use design inputs to enable simple assembly and field usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation aids, training, and usability testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide comprehensive IFU, scoring aids, and training materials and demonstrate usability by naïve operators and field staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare instructions for use, interpretation spreadsheet (Excel), photographs/video for training; test on naïve operators to optimize. Evaluate operability at field sites and refine IFU/training accordingly. Provide a simple scoring chart and downloadable interpretation tools to improve objectivity and record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality System / Design Control and regulatory planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop product under formal quality systems and plan regulatory strategy appropriate to intended claims (surveillance vs diagnostic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage project per ISO13485 and Design Control guidelines; as manufacturer follows GMP. For population surveillance use, products historically may be exempt from FDA review (waiver/exemption), but diagnostic claims will require FDA clearance; plan validation and documentation accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparator and statistical performance thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Define statistical thresholds for comparisons versus reference assays and for lot/product acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concordance/correlation metrics (e.g., >95% correspondence; prototype data cited >98% agreement for some panels). Define pass criteria for lab validation (e.g., %CV <10%), and set clear acceptance criteria for mean duration, FRR, and lot QC performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of exclusions or reflex testing
rubrics_metrics.description: If assay performance (especially FRR) is suboptimal in certain populations, plan for exclusion criteria or reflex algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FRR >2% in a population, consider excluding that population or implementing a recent infection test algorithm (RITA) that reflexes 'recents' to another incidence assay, clinical data, CD4, or HIV RNA to reduce misclassification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical design choices to avoid assay artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Assay chemistry and conjugate design must avoid non-specific associations and migration/agglutination artifacts on membranes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hydrophilized synthetic peptides (vs large hydrophobic recombinant proteins) and hydrophilic linkers for conjugation to improve solubility and reduce nonspecific association. Small sizes of HRP-labeled conjugates and peptide capture conjugates reduce agglutination and migration issues in lateral flow membranes.
